UFMR and PC-FMR have comparable diagnostic performance for detection of breast lesions in patients who have breast cancer.
the diagnostic performance of fusion of DWI and unenhanced or postcontrast T1W imaging is similar in patients with breast malignancy.

the diagnostic performance of DWI using unenhanced (UDWI) or early postgadolinium T1-weighted MR imaging (PDWI) to detect and differentiate breast lesions in patients undergoing breast cancer treatment was similar.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diagnostic performance of UFMR or PCMR for breast lesions in patients who have breast cancer.
the fusion of diffusion-weighted images using unenhanced or postcontrast T1- weighted MR images in breast cancer.
the diagnostic performance of fusion DWI using UFMR or PCMR in patients with breast lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both UFMR and postcontrast FMR can be used to characterize breast lesions in women with breast cancer.
both UFMR and early PCFMR are useful for detecting and characterizing breast lesions in patients suspected with breast cancer.
fused DWI using either UFMR or PCMR could be used for the detection of breast lesions in patients undergoing breast MRI for breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fused DWI with PCFMR could be used as an alternative to the fused DWI using UFMR to detect and characterize the breast lesions.

the fusion of diffusion-weighted imaging using either unenhanded or postcontrast T1-weighed imaging could be used to detect and characterize lesions with similar accuracy in patients with breast cancers, although the conspicuity of lesions is better with postcontrast images.
the diagnostic performance of DWI using UFMR or PCMR was similar in patients with breast cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UFMR is as accurate as PCFMR for detecting and characterizing breast lesions in patients who are undergoing breast cancer surgery.
the diagnostic performance of breast MRI with DWI using unenhanced or postcontrast T1W images for detection, characterization, and assessment of breast lesions is similar.
UFMR is an alternative to postcontrast imaging for breast DWI.
